problem_statement: This is the VitePress documentation site for the vite-plugin-pwa project: a landing home page at /, and documentation sections rendered from Markdown under /guide/ (Getting Started), /frameworks/ (Frameworks) and /deployment/ (Deployment), all wrapped in the shared VitePress doc layout (left sidebar navigation, a content column and a right aside/outline). The docs team wants the site's own on-page navigation improved so every documentation section ends with a compact 'On this page' section navigator: a labelled row of green jump chips linking to that page's real headings, with the first section highlighted, styled to read as part of the green VitePress docs brand. They also want a small 'Release line' picker in the always-present right aside (Stable / Next / LTS) with a live readout naming which release line the reader is following. Ship it so it (1) appears at the bottom of the Guide (/guide/), Frameworks (/frameworks/) AND Deployment (/deployment/) documentation pages alike (a shared component rendered from the docs layout, not a per-page copy), (2) lays out its jump-chip row responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px), (3) matches the green VitePress docs styling (light-green panel, green chips, a high-contrast dark-on-green active chip) rather than an off-brand dark-slate slab, a collapsed label overlapping the chips, or a pale-on-pale illegible active chip, and (4) keeps the release-line readout in sync with the picker so a reader who switches to the Next line sees the readout update to 'Following: Next release line' rather than a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the site - the sidebar navigation, the dark-mode toggle, the existing docs copy and the VitePress build - intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'On this page' section navigator at the bottom of the documentation pages so it renders on the Guide (/guide/), Frameworks (/frameworks/) AND Deployment (/deployment/) pages (a shared component rendered from the docs layout, not a per-page copy).
The navigator shows an 'On this page' label and a row of jump chips linking to the current page's real section headings, with the first section highlighted as the active chip.
The jump-chip row must wrap responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the navigator in the green VitePress docs language (light-green panel, green chips, a high-contrast dark-on-green active chip). Do NOT ship an off-brand dark-slate slab, a label that collapses onto and overlaps the chip row, or a pale-on-pale illegible active chip.

Add a 'Release line' picker (Stable / Next / LTS) in the always-present right aside with a readout, and wire it so that after clicking the Next chip the readout reads 'Following: Next release line' - it must re-read the live selection, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the sidebar navigation, the dark-mode toggle, the existing docs copy and the VitePress build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the 'On this page' section navigator as a shared component rendered from the VitePress docs layout (the doc-after slot) so a single source of truth reaches every documentation page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.

The jump-chip row must use a fluid, wrapping, responsive flex layout (flex-wrap:wrap, min-width:0 on chips, consistent gap spacing, no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet (834px) or mobile (390px).

The navigator must adopt the VitePress green docs theme and visual style: a light-green (#effdf5) rounded panel with a green left border (#42b883), an uppercase small-caps green label typography, white pill-button chips with a mint (#d9fbe8) border, and a HIGH-CONTRAST active chip that is dark text (#052e16) on solid brand green (#42b883). Do not ship an off-brand dark-slate slab, a pale-mint-on-pale-mint illegible active chip, or a label pulled by a negative margin so it overlaps the chip row.

Place the release-line picker (Stable / Next / LTS pill-button chips plus a monospace readout) in the always-present right aside beneath the outline, separate from the navigator, matching the aside's type scale and spacing, and make the readout reflect the CURRENT selection after every click by reading the live selected line, so it can never go stale relative to the highlighted chip.
Do not remove or regress the left sidebar navigation, the dark-mode toggle, the existing docs copy, the right aside outline or the VitePress build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the home landing page across viewports.
desktop_guide, mobile_guide, desktop_frameworks and desktop_deployment protect the existing documentation pages and must carry the Release readiness rail at the bottom.
desktop_rail_guide and mobile_rail_guide scroll the Release readiness rail into view and must show the green rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_frameworks protects the rail's presence on the Frameworks documentation page.
channel_toggle_guide clicks the Next chip in the release-line picker; the readout must then read 'Following: Next release line'.

change_completion: The Release readiness rail is present at the bottom of the Guide, Frameworks AND Deployment pages (the shared component reaches all three documentation sections).

After clicking the Next chip in the release-line picker on the Guide page, the readout updates to 'Following: Next release line' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Following: Stable release line'.
design_consistency: The rail on the rail states matches the reference's green docs styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-brand slab.
The rail adopts the green VitePress brand tokens and light-panel idiom so it reads as part of the docs across every page.
responsive: No captured docs page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tile row wraps.
desktop_rail_guide, mobile_rail_guide and desktop_rail_frameworks keep the Release readiness rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The sidebar navigation and the dark-mode toggle remain present and functional.
The existing docs copy and the VitePress build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

author_notes: slot_191 DEDUP + L4 hardening onto the antfu vite-plugin-pwa VitePress documentation site (reassigned off the shared MarketingPipeline Simply-Docs repo to remove a triple duplicate). The docs build is a standalone VitePress render of the project's own docs/ workspace; the shared markdown copy, the VitePress sidebar navigation, the dark-mode toggle and the green brand tokens are byte-identical across legs. The L4 levers ride on a new shared ReleaseReadinessRail component rendered from the docs layout's doc-after slot plus a ReleaseChannelPicker readout host in the always-present aside-top slot. reference = rail on all three documentation sections, fluid wrap, green light-panel styling, and a channel readout that re-reads the live selection (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the original unrepaired rail: present on the Guide section only (fails D2 cross-page on the Frameworks/Deployment pages), a fixed 820px nowrap tile row (fails D6 mobile overflow ~479px), an off-brand dark-slate slab (fails D3 visual), but its channel readout IS synced on click (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' rail: present on the Guide only (fails D2 on Frameworks/Deployment), a 600px min-width nowrap row with a shallow inner overflow-x:hidden non-fix (fails D6 mobile ~295px), an off-palette amber card (fails D3), and a channel readout wired from a value snapshotted once at setup so it stays 'Stable' after switching to Next (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The VitePress build renders every documentation page fully static with sponsors imagery localised and the algolia search widget removed, so every leg is offline-clean.
